public_rationale: The condition held on a fair reading. ChatGPT went from 500M weekly users at end of March 2025 to 800M by October 6, about 48M a month. That matches or beats the roughly 43M a month from August 2024 to March 2025. The first prediction came true. In August 2025 Altman said OpenAI had to make 'capacity tradeoffs' and ration compute after GPT-5 demand. The second part did not hold. OpenAI's CFO said compute rose from 0.6 GW in 2024 to 1.9 GW in 2025, so OpenAI had plenty of room to expand. The capacity part holds; the expansion part fails.
limitations: If 'this rate' means the faster Feb-Mar 2025 spike (about 75M/month), growth later slowed, and the condition would not be met.
The compute figures are OpenAI's own claims.

statement.excerpt: If OpenAI's growth continues at this rate, it will run into capacity issues, and it does not have much room to expand.
statement.document_title: OpenAI Is A Systemic Risk To The Tech Industry

from_speaker: If OpenAI's growth continues at this rate
it will run into capacity issues
it does not have much room to expand
our_interpretation: 'This rate' refers to ChatGPT's weekly-user growth up to 500 million at end of March 2025. He gave no specific rate. I use the average from August 2024 (200M) to end of March 2025 (500M), about 43M users a month, and treat the condition as met if later growth stayed at about that pace.
'Run into capacity issues' read plainly: OpenAI publicly reports compute shortages that force rate limits, tradeoffs, or delays.

'Does not have much room to expand' read plainly: OpenAI could not substantially grow its compute capacity. It is tested against how much capacity OpenAI actually added in 2025, not against signed future deals.
criteria.support_condition: Growth continued at about the earlier pace, and OpenAI reported capacity shortfalls and failed to expand compute substantially.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Growth continued at about the earlier pace, but OpenAI had no notable capacity problems, or it expanded compute substantially.

evidence.explanation: The same article reports 800M weekly users on Oct 6, 2025. That is 300M added in about 6.2 months after end of March, about 48M a month, at or above the earlier average pace.

evidence.explanation: 400M in Feb 2025 was double August 2024 (200M). From August 2024 to 500M at end of March 2025 is about 43M a month, the baseline used for 'this rate'.

evidence.excerpt: CEO Sam Altman says the company will be forced to make “capacity tradeoffs”
evidence.explanation: In August 2025, after continued growth, OpenAI said capacity was strained and it had to ration compute. This bears out the 'will run into capacity issues' part.

evidence.publisher: Reuters (via The Star), reporting OpenAI CFO blog
evidence.explanation: OpenAI roughly tripled its compute capacity in 2025. That contradicts 'does not have much room to expand'.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: OpenAI reported its 2025 compute capacity at about triple 2024. That settles the room-to-expand part; the capacity-issues part was settled by e3.
